formal_statement: ∀ (P L : ℕ) (inc : Fin P → Fin L → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit), PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.IsMonotoneCircuit C → ∀ (j a b : ℕ) (op : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp), (op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨ op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or) → C.gates[j]? = some ⟨op, [a, b]⟩ → a < P + L + j → b < P + L + j → ∀ (w : Fin L) (y : Fin P), PEqualNP.LowMerge.IsLow P L inc C (P + L + j) w → y ∈ PEqualNP.LowMerge.aliveSet P L C (P + L + j) w → (PEqualNP.LowMerge.IsLow P L inc C a w ∧ y ∈ PEqualNP.LowMerge.aliveSet P L C a w) ∨ (PEqualNP.LowMerge.IsLow P L inc C b w ∧ y ∈ PEqualNP.LowMerge.aliveSet P L C b w)
plain_statement: Points then lines are the inputs; inc says which point lies on which line. A wire is low for a line w when, with w the only line on, it is true only on point sets containing a point of w; its alive set at w is the set of points p where it is true with only p and w on. In a circuit of AND and OR gates only, if gate h is the AND or the OR of exactly two earlier wires a and b, h is low for w, and y is in the alive set of h at w, then a or b is low for w with y in its alive set at w.
title: Pair passing for low wires: in an AND/OR circuit, a low AND or OR of two earlier wires passes each point of its alive set to a low operand
